subject: Helios discovery — model shortlist, perf baselines, and quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@helios.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helios discovery — model shortlist, perf baselines, and quantization tradeoffs

Hi Lina and Rajiv,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation and helpful context on the three core user flows you highlighted (entity extraction from analyst notes, short-form summarization for executive reviews, and conversational Q&A over your proprietary datasets). Below is a concise recap, our recommended POC plan, and a short note on quantization tradeoffs so you can decide what to prioritize for the initial evaluation.

Recap (quick)
- Goals: match human-level precision on entity extraction (F1 target >= 0.88), fast per-document summarization (<500ms median for 2k tokens), and high factuality for Q&A.
- Constraints: on-prem sandbox for July POC, strict data retention + audit needs, procurement expects commercial terms by mid-July.

Model shortlist (recommended for POC)
1) Mistral-1-70B-chat (FP16 baseline) — best quality/latency balance for summarization and extraction.
2) Llama-2-70B-chat (AWQ 4-bit variant) — lower cost, slightly lower benched F1 on extraction (~1.5-3% gap) but much higher throughput when quantized.
3) Falcon-40B-instruct (FP16 / GPTQ) — strong Q&A; smaller mem footprint but mixed summarization results on our tests.

Benchmarks & prompt sets
- Attached: helios-poc-benchmarks.csv (slice-level metrics: F1, ROUGE-L, median latency for 512/2048 tokens)
- Prompt set: helios-prompt-set-v1.txt — includes extraction templates, summarization instruction prompts, and Q&A seeds pulled from your sample corpus you shared in the call.
- Public perf gist (internal): https://gist.github.com/redwood/helios-poc-benchmarks

Quantization / throughput summary (short)
- AWQ (4-bit) on Llama-family: +2.5–3.5x throughput vs FP16, observed 1.5–3% drop in extraction F1 in our Helios slices. Good first pass when latency/cost is primary.
- GPTQ (4-bit) on Falcon: +2x throughput, typically preserves quality better on instruction tuning tasks but requires per-model calibration; larger variance across slices.
- FP8 (experimental on select runtimes): can approach FP16 quality with ~1.3x speedup on supported hardware, but limited availability on private infra and toolchain.

Suggested POC plan (2 weeks)
1) Run targeted evals (we'll run): Mistral-1-70B (FP16), Llama-2-70B (AWQ-4), Falcon-40B (GPTQ-4) on the provided Helios sample (we'll use 500 doc eval set from your corpus).
2) Measure per-slice metrics (we've attached the initial CSV) and a short qualitative review for factuality.
3) If AWQ shows <1.5% degradation vs FP16 on extraction, we'll propose an AWQ canary for the application path and compute cost delta/projections.

Immediate asks from your side
- Share the 500-doc eval set in the same S3/GCS folder (or let us grab from the same Drive link you shared).
- Confirm any additional redlines for data processing or retention for the sandbox.

Next steps
- I'll upload the full benchmark outputs and a short 1-page tradeoff doc (quant-tradeoffs-summary.pdf) by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute deep dive next Tue (6/22) to review the POC outputs and agree on a canary config.

Thanks — happy to adapt the plan if you'd prefer a slower-but-higher-quality approach first.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

Attachments: helios-poc-benchmarks.csv (CSV), helios-prompt-set-v1.txt (TXT), quant-tradeoffs-summary.pdf (PDF)

Thanks, Stephanie — this is helpful and the level of detail is great. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we hand the eval set over to you:  

1) Quality regression sensitivity: our legal/compliance team is particularly sensitive to extraction errors that could affect downstream billing; can you quantify the failure modes you saw on the 1.5–3% drop for AWQ? In particular, were errors biased toward certain entity types or long-form notes?

2) Canary strategy: if AWQ is the cheaper option and we see a ~2% F1 drop, what safe rollout path do you recommend for us to protect customer-facing pipelines?

3) On infra: our sandbox will be an on-prem GPU node (A100 equivalent) with limited admin access. Do you expect behavior differences vs your hosted runs?

We can share the 500-doc eval set once we confirm the NDAs/procurement gating for the on-prem transfer. Also looping Rajiv for procurement timelines.

Best,
Lina

Ben / Aditya — forwarding Lina's clarifying questions. TL;DR notes and recommended next actions for our POC run: 

TL;DR from benched slices
- AWQ 4-bit (Llama-2-70B-chat): ~2.2% absolute F1 regression on extraction vs FP16 on the Helios slices we ran; errors skewed toward nested entity boundaries and very long notes (>2.5k tokens).
- GPTQ 4-bit (Falcon-40B): ~1.1% F1 regression, more stable on nested entities but slower per-token throughput than AWQ on our infra.
- Mistral FP16: baseline quality highest, but cost ~2.8x vs AWQ Llama for same throughput.

Recommended canary path (safe, incremental):
1) Start with Llama-2-70B (AWQ-4) in a read-only evaluation canary that serves 10% of non-critical traffic (internal analytics only) for 48 hours and run automated drift/regression checks on the extraction outputs.
2) If drift/regression metrics show <1.5% delta and no high-severity factuality regressions in the qualitative audit, expand to 40% for 72 hours with automated rollback on detected anomalies.
3) Keep Mistral FP16 as fallback and set routing policy with faster failover (1s timeout) to avoid client-visible latency spikes.

Infra notes for on-prem sandbox
- AWQ throughput depends heavily on library support; on A100-equivalent hardware AWQ shows similar raw throughput to our hosted numbers but you should expect slightly higher latency variance under multi-tenant loads. We recommend isolating the POC node where possible.
- We will prepare a minimal runtime bundle (container + small calibration artifact) to run on your sandbox; it requires limited admin rights to the GPU driver but not full cluster privileges.

Action items I can own this week
- Provide a short calibration script + instructions for running AWQ/GPTQ on your sandbox.
- Run the three-model eval using the 500-doc set once you confirm transfer permissions.

Leaving suggested language for procurement (Rajiv) to speed NDA/data transfer.

-Steph
